title: Here, in the Broken Bread
description: Here, in the Broken Bread in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Henry Furness wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 682 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “A Communion Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Here, in the bro-ken bread, Here, in the cup we take, His bo-dy and his blood be-hold, Who suff-ered for our sake.

lines: Here, in the cup we take,
His body and his blood behold,
Father, what more couldst thou have done
Than thou hast done for us?
Thy children from thy boundless love,
Who died to make us sure
And from the power and pains of sin

licence: Public domain: William Henry Furness died in 1896.
credits: Words by William Henry Furness (1802–1896), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
